entities.name: Michalon Lituanus
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Michalon Lituanus (b. 1490) was a Baltic explorer and navigator of the Late Middle Ages, shaping the maritime trade between the Grand Duchy of Lithuania and the Hanseatic League.

As a key figure in the medieval Baltic region, Michalon Lituanus played a crucial role in the establishment of trade routes between Lithuania and the Scandinavian kingdoms, facilitating the exchange of goods such as amber, wax, and furs.

His contributions to the region's economic development were significant, as he helped to create a network of trade routes that connected the Baltic coast to the wider European economy.

Michalon Lituanus's legacy can be seen in the continued importance of the Baltic Sea as a major trade route in modern times, and his name remains a testament to the enduring influence of the Grand Duchy of Lithuania on the region's history and culture.

The inscription on the Michalon Lituanus Monument in Vilnius reads: 'Though time may pass, the spirit of our ancestors will always be remembered.'
